strings: A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A cheap bar of soap. Doesn't smell.
A metal tray to lay food on.
It has a large ketchup smear on it.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
This is the adorable by-product of multiple attempts at genetically mixing mothpeople with cockroaches.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
Ropes that are meant to go around a wrestling ring.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
Now you see me, now you don't...
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
Directs energy into compressed particles in order to power engines.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A heap of dense garbage. Perhaps there is something interesting inside?
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
Used to order supplies, approve requests, and control the shuttle.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
Go back. Go back. Go back. Can you operate the elevator.
Indicates what floor the elevator is at and which way it's going.
Keeps idiots like you from walking into an open elevator shaft.
A canister for the storage of gas.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
A case of classy Havanian cigars.
A case of imported Cohiba cigars, renowned for their strong flavor.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A portable variant of the station scrubbers, capable of filtering gas from the air around it or inserted tank. May also be wrenched into a port.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
A remote control switch for a mounted flasher.
A telescreen that connects to the isolation cells camera network.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
A coil of insulated power cable.
Contains condensed capsaicin for use in law \"enforcement.\"
This relatively unknown vending machine delivers clothing for Atmospherics Technicians, an equally unknown job.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A remote control switch for a mechanical curtain.
They look like tracks left by wheels.
A window made out of a plasma-silicate alloy and a rod matrix. It looks hopelessly tough to break and is most likely nigh fireproof.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
The floor you walk on. It looks near-impervious to damage.
This station is just crawling with bugs.

An industrial unit made to hold, charge, and decontaminate equipment. It comes with a built-in UV cauterization mechanism. A small warning label advises that organic matter should not be placed into the unit.
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
Damn, they better have the /tg/ channel on these things.
Perfectly designed to be comfortable to sit on, and hellish to sleep on.
Contains a large reservoir of soft drinks.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
It's green and acidic. It looks like... blood?
An all-terrain vehicle built for traversing rough terrain with ease. This one looks rather old and well used, it's original company logo scratched out and repainted with the name Assistant Shredder.
Checked out books MUST be returned on time.
For art pieces hung by the public.
A portable generator for emergency backup power.
No matter how much you squirm, it'll still be uncomfortable.
A full tile window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A coil of pipe cleaners. Good for arts and crafts, not to build with.
Draw out your soul on this canvas!
Breaking and making art since 4000 BC. This one uses advanced technology to allow the creation of lifelike moving statues.
For the hard-working tradesperson who's in the middle of nowhere and just wants to warm up their pastry-based savoury item from an overpriced vending machine.
You can use this to wrap items in.
A combined label printer, applicator, and remover, all in a single portable device. Designed to be easy to operate and use.
Somehow, you can always find one under the wrestling ring.
An underfloor disposal pipe with a sorting mechanism.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with identification modification programs.
They look like human remains. They have a strange aura about them.
A vending machine which dispenses hot drinks.
The HU-452, an experimental urinal. Comes complete with experimental urinal cake.
Made by Space Amish using traditional space techniques, this heater/cooler is guaranteed not to set the station on fire. Warranty void if used in engines.
A remote control switch for a mass driver.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
It's a big crowbar. It doesn't fit in your pockets, because it's big.
A machine that processes and routes PDA and request console messages.
A small crowbar. This handy tool is useful for lots of things, such as prying floor tiles or opening unpowered doors.
A piece of headgear used in dangerous working conditions to protect the head. Comes with a built-in flashlight.
A cheap Nanotrasen security laptop, it functions as a security records console. It's bolted to the table.
Used to access the station's automated alert system.
A telescreen with access to the research division's camera network.
A nicely-crafted wooden dresser. It's filled with lots of undies.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
This device recharges energy-dependent lifeforms, like cyborgs, ethereals, and MODsuit users.
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.
For masterpieces hand-picked by the curator.
A shooting target that looks like a xenomorphic alien.
A shooting target that looks like a useless clown.
A shooting target that looks like syndicate scum.
A secure crate containing various materials for building a customised test-site.
A set of Nanotrasen regulations for keeping law, order, and procedure followed within their space stations.
An adorable stuffed toy that resembles a round, fluffy looking bird. Not to be mistaken for his friend, the birb plushie.
A sign labelling an area where research and science is performed.
It's a normal red ink pen.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
